_readme: Machine-readable register of every official rule figure the public guide publishes.
Each record was re-opened at its source URL on the check date recorded in 'checked'.
A record here verifies LAW, an official benchmark, or an official statistic. It never
verifies a household value, an appraisal, a premium, a bill or a projection.
Values are the official published numbers. Where the guide displays a rounded form
($10 rounding rule), 'display_rounded' records the rounded text that appears on the site
and 'official_exact' keeps the source value so a reader can match the two.
Do not add a record without a source_url that was actually opened and read.

figures.claim: Federal basic exclusion amount for estates of decedents dying in 2026
figures.note: IR-2026-133 (Nov. 5, 2026) confirms $15,000,000 for 2026 and $15,480,000 for 2027. The 'What's new' page attributes the $15,000,000 amount to Public Law 119-21 (signed July 4, 2025).

figures.claim: Federal basic exclusion amount for estates of decedents dying in 2027
figures.note: IR-2026-133, 'Estate Tax Exclusion', states $15,480,000 for 2027 deaths, up from $15,000,000 for 2026.

figures.claim: Form 706 filing test: gross estate plus adjusted taxable gifts plus specific gift tax exemption compared with the filing threshold
figures.note: The IRS page states a filing is required if the gross estate, increased by adjusted taxable gifts and specific gift tax exemption, exceeds the filing threshold for the year of death. Deductions reduce the taxable estate, not the filing test. This distinction is why no household headroom can be published.

figures.claim: No California estate tax return is required for decedents dying on or after 1 January 2005
figures.note: Re-read 15 Nov 2026: the Controller's page states the state death tax credit was eliminated effective 1 January 2005 and that no California Estate Tax Return is required for decedents dying on or after that date.

figures.claim: California does not impose an inheritance tax on beneficiaries for modern deaths
figures.note: Same Controller page: the Inheritance Tax is collected only for decedents who died prior to June 8, 1982. The federal estate tax, not a state inheritance tax, is the exposure to test.

figures.claim: Basis of inherited property is generally fair market value on the date of death, or the alternate valuation date if the executor elects it on a timely Form 706
figures.note: Alternate valuation requires an estate tax return and an election. Rev. Rul. 2023-2 is the exception example the guide cites for a grantor-trust fact pattern outside the estate.

figures.claim: Exclusion of up to $250,000 of gain on sale of a main home ($500,000 on a qualifying joint return), subject to ownership and use tests
figures.note: Ownership test: owned at least 24 of the last 60 months. Use test: used as residence at least 24 of the previous 60 months. The exclusion is not automatic.

figures.claim: Proposition 19 intergenerational transfer value allowance for transfers 16 Feb 2025 through 15 Feb 2027
figures.note: BOE LTA 2025/009 sets $1,044,586 using the 2.15% FHFA California HPI change for 2024. The site displays the nearest-$10 form, $1,044,590, and labels it as rounded. Prior periods: $1,000,000 (16 Feb 2021 - 15 Feb 2023) and $1,022,600 (16 Feb 2023 - 15 Feb 2025). The next adjustment occurs February 2027 and its amount is unknown.

figures.claim: Family-home relief requires the transferee to occupy the home as a principal residence within one year and to file the homeowners' or disabled veterans' exemption within one year of transfer for exclusion from the transfer date
figures.note: A late exemption claim gives prospective relief only, beginning the year the claim is filed. Renting the home instead of occupying it does not meet the family-home condition.

figures.claim: BOE-19-P claim is due within three years of transfer and before transfer to a third party, and is also timely if filed within six months of the supplemental or escape assessment notice
figures.note: Re-read 15 Nov 2026 alongside the Board's Proposition 19 comparison chart, which states the exclusion claim period as within 3 years or before a transfer to a third party.

figures.claim: Proposition 13 limits the annual inflation adjustment to a property's factored base year value to no more than 2%, and the assessor enrolls the lower of factored base year value or market value
figures.note: BOE LTA 2025/023 (Pub 800-10 information sheet) also warns that a property in Proposition 8 decline-in-value status can rise more than 2% on a later lien date, though never above its factored base year value.

figures.claim: Official Proposition 13 inflation factor for the 2026-27 assessment year
figures.note: LTA 2026/002 (Jan. 13, 2026) sets the factor at 1.02. California CPI rose 3.307% (Aug 2024 to Aug 2025, substituting for unavailable October data after the fall 2025 federal shutdown); the 2% constitutional cap applies. The same LTA publishes the full 1976-77 to 2026-27 factor history used on the real-conditions page.

figures.claim: Of the 51 published assessment years 1976-77 through 2026-27, the factor reached the full 2% cap in 40 years (78%) and compounded at about 1.81% a year
figures.note: Derived by counting the rows of the enclosed factor table in LTA 2026/002. Factors below 2% occurred in 1983-84 and 1995-96 through 2004-05 in part, and in 2010-11 (negative), 2011-12, 2014-15, 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2021-22. This is a count of official published values, not a forecast.

figures.claim: San Francisco secured property tax rate for fiscal year 2026-27
figures.note: Treasurer & Tax Collector page states the FY 2026-27 secured rate is 1.18162182%. Direct charges and special assessments can be additional. The model holds this rate constant as a scenario; the page does not forecast future rates.

figures.claim: Allowable annual rent increase for covered units, 1 March 2026 through 28 February 2027
figures.note: SF Rent Board report. Applicability depends on the unit being covered and on correct notice. The same page carries the 9 Nov 2026 notice that File 261020 is proposed and not enacted.

figures.claim: Proposed ordinance File 261020 to limit combined banked and capital-improvement increases is not enacted as of the 9 Nov 2026 notice
figures.note: The Rent Board page states: 'This legislation has not been enacted and is subject to change.' The guide therefore treats it as a watchlist item, not current law.

figures.claim: Where an interest in real property is transferred by reason of death, including through a trust, the change in ownership statement must be filed within 150 days after the date of death
figures.note: Revenue and Taxation Code section 480(b) names trust transfers expressly and places the duty on the trustee (if the property was held in trust) or the transferee. Probate estates use the inventory-and-appraisal timing instead.

figures.claim: Trustee notification must be served not later than 60 days following the triggering event, subject to the section's exceptions
figures.note: Probate Code section 16061.7(f). The 60-day period starts later if there is a trustee vacancy. Not every trust triggers the same notice or deadline, so the guide says so.

figures.claim: H.R. 1301 (119th Congress) was introduced 13 Feb 2025 and referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means; it has not been enacted
figures.official_exact: Introduced; referred to Ways and Means
figures.note: Re-read 16 Nov 2026 on Congress.gov (after a 15 Nov read): Rep. Randy Feenstra [R-IA-4], introduced 13 Feb 2025; House Ways and Means; the latest action on the page remains the 13 Feb 2025 referral; tracker status 'Introduced'; CBO cost estimates listed as zero. Repeal of the estate tax and the GST tax is a proposal at step 1 of 5, not law.

figures.claim: SB 284 (2025-2026) remains an active bill in committee and has not been enacted
figures.note: Re-read 16 Nov 2026 on leginfo (after a 15 Nov read): status 'Active Bill - In Committee Process'; House Location: Assembly; last amended 25 Jun 2025; latest history action 14 Jul 2025, 'Set, final hearing. Held in committee and under submission.' The measure would amend R&T Code §63.2 and add §63.2.1. Proposal, not law.

figures.claim: CPI-U rose 6.5% over the 12 months ending December 2022; electricity rose 14.3% over the same period
figures.note: BLS archived release USDL-23-0017, Table A, unadjusted 12-month changes. Used only to show that a single inflation rate can miss wide divergence between categories.

figures.claim: Annual-average CPI-U change from 1991 through 2025: arithmetic mean 2.62%, median 2.63%, standard deviation 1.41%, range -0.36% (2009) to 8.00% (2022); 10 of 34 years above 3%
figures.note: Computed from the annual-average CPIAUCNS series (BLS data via FRED), downloaded 13 Nov 2026, annual averages 1990-2025. The arithmetic is reproducible from the published series; the statistics themselves are a derived summary, not an official BLS statistic. The 2026 year is incomplete and is excluded.

figures.claim: CBO's February 2026 baseline projects PCE inflation returning to roughly 2% in 2030 and stabilizing thereafter, over a 2026-2036 horizon
figures.note: CBO publication 61882, The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036. The horizon ends in 2036. Nothing in it is a 50-year housing or portfolio forecast, and the guide says so.

figures.claim: 72% probability of at least one magnitude 6.7 or greater earthquake somewhere in the San Francisco Bay region between 2014 and 2043
figures.note: USGS Fact Sheet 2016-3020. It is a regional probability, not the probability of loss at a particular parcel, and it does not price damage or insurance.

figures.claim: Freddie Mac PMMS 30-year fixed rate averaged 7.11% as of 12 November 2026
figures.note: Weekly survey average of applications. Recorded as an observed benchmark only. The guide models no mortgage, so this does not enter any projection.

figures.claim: Cupertino water is supplied through three separate systems: California Water Service (northeast), San Jose Water Company (southeast), and the City-owned system operated by San Jose Water Company under lease (west)
figures.note: This is why a ZIP code alone cannot establish a water bill, and why the guide leaves water amounts blank rather than publishing an estimate.

figures.claim: Santa Clara County documentary transfer tax is $0.55 per $500 of value, equivalent to $1.10 per $1,000
figures.official_exact: $0.55 per $500 or fractional portion of real property value
figures.note: Re-read 15 Nov 2026 on the county page: the tax is due on all changes of ownership unless an applicable statutory exemption is cited; a missing Preliminary Change of Ownership Report adds $20; the city add-on rate named on the page applies to San Jose, Palo Alto and Mountain View.

figures.claim: Maximum FDIC deposit insurance coverage for a trust owner with five or more beneficiaries
figures.official_exact: $1,250,000 per owner for all trust accounts at the same bank
figures.note: FDIC 'Your Insured Deposits': as of April 1, 2024 the maximum coverage for a trust owner with five or more beneficiaries is $1,250,000 per owner for all trust accounts (POD/ITF, revocable and irrevocable) held at the same bank. The page also states coverage does not cover investments, even if bought at an insured bank.

figures.claim: Homeowners' exemption claim on a Proposition 19 family home must be filed within one year of the transfer
figures.note: BOE Proposition 19 page, 'Filing Period' row of the parent-child comparison chart, read 15 Nov 2026: 'File for homeowners' exemption within 1 year of transfer' and 'File claim for exclusion within 3 years or before transfer to third party'. Replaces the earlier note that the periods were not re-read.

figures.claim: Form 1041 income tax returns of estates and trusts are due on or before the 15th day of the fourth month after the close of the tax year
figures.note: 26 U.S.C. 6072(a), read 15 Nov 2026 (Cornell LII copy of the United States Code): returns under sections 6012, 6013 or 6017 on a calendar year are due on or before 15 April following the close of the calendar year, and on a fiscal year by the 15th day of the fourth month following the close. The IRS Instructions for Form 1041 were not read, so the fiscal year a decedent's estate may elect is not published on the site.

figures.claim: Santa Clara County charges an additional $20 when a required Preliminary Change of Ownership Report is not completed, signed and submitted at recording
figures.note: County Clerk-Recorder 'Recording real estate' page, read 15 Nov 2026. The page states the PCOR is available through the county forms site and that the $20 is due if the report is required but missing at recording.

figures.claim: California's top individual rate for 2025 is 12.30%, beginning above $742,953 of taxable income for single filers, $1,485,906 for married filing jointly, and $1,010,417 for head of household
figures.note: Read directly from the 2025 California Tax Rate Schedules PDF on 15 Nov 2026: Schedule X 12.30% at and over $742,953; Schedule Y 12.30% at and over $1,485,906; Schedule Z 12.30% at and over $1,010,417. These are published government thresholds, so the site shows them exactly instead of rounding them to $10; the $10 rule applies to household and model amounts.

figures.claim: The 1% Behavioral Health Services Tax (R&TC §17043) applies to taxable income above $1,000,000, for any filing status; the threshold is not indexed
figures.note: Re-opened and read on 15 Nov 2026 by session 24158ab3: §17043(a) states 'an additional tax shall be imposed at the rate of 1 percent on that portion of a taxpayer's taxable income in excess of one million dollars ($1,000,000)'. The statute text on the official California Legislative Information page is the source; the $1,000,000 figure is the published statutory threshold, so it is shown exactly rather than rounded.

figures.claim: California Form 540 line 62 Behavioral Health Services Tax: 1% on California taxable income above $1,000,000, computed on the whole-dollar excess; added on top of the regular rate schedule
figures.note: FTB 2025 Instructions for Form 540, Line 62, read 15 Nov 2026: taxable income from line 19 less $1,000,000, multiplied by 1%. The Mental Health Services Act was renamed the Behavioral Health Services Act for taxable years beginning on or after 1 January 2025 (FTB Tax News, March 2026). California taxes capital gains as ordinary income, so a large gain pushing taxable income above $1M faces the 12.3% top bracket plus this 1% surcharge (13.3% combined on that slice).

figures.claim: California does not grant a preferential rate for long-term capital gains; gains are taxed as ordinary income under the graduated rate schedule, subject to the 1% Behavioral Health Services Tax above $1,000,000
figures.note: FTB 2025 Form 540 instructions, read 15 Nov 2026: California computes tax on California taxable income using the rate schedules; capital gains are included in ordinary income. Combined with CA-RATE-SCHEDULE-2025 and CA-BHST-1M, the top combined marginal rate on a gain above $1M of taxable income is 13.3% (12.30% + 1.00%).

figures.claim: Santa Clara County publishes a Compilation of Tax Rates & Information each fiscal year; the rate is limited to 1% of assessed value plus voter-approved bond indebtedness, and the county is divided into 816 Tax Rate Areas whose first two digits identify the city or unincorporated area; the lien date is January 1
figures.official_exact: 1% base + bonds; 816 TRAs; lien date Jan 1
figures.display_rounded: 1% base + bonds; 816 TRAs; lien date Jan 1
figures.note: SCC Controller-Treasurer Property Tax Rate Book page, read 15 Nov 2026. The FY2025-26 book states the 1% limit, voter-approved bond add-ons, 816 Tax Rate Areas, and January 1 lien date. The exact TRA rate for a specific parcel cannot be read from the published book without the parcel's TRA number; the bill's effective rate (including direct charges) is owner-stated and flagged.

figures.claim: Enacted Proposition 19 value-cap allowance windows: $1,000,000 for 16 Feb 2021 – 15 Feb 2023; $1,022,600 for 16 Feb 2023 – 15 Feb 2025; $1,044,586 for 16 Feb 2025 – 15 Feb 2027
figures.note: BOE LTA 2025/009 enclosure table, re-read 15 Nov 2026. The letter states the adjustment mechanism (Cal. Const. art. XIII A section 2.1(c)(4)): every other February 16 the BOE adjusts the $1,000,000 amount to reflect the percentage change in the FHFA House Price Index for California for the prior calendar year; the 2024 change was 2.15%. The next adjustment occurs February 2027 and its amount is not yet published.

figures.claim: 26 U.S.C. 1031 covers exchanges of real property held for productive use or investment for like-kind real property; 45-day identification and 180-day completion (or return due date)
figures.note: Statutory text read 15 Nov 2026 on the Cornell LII copy: section 1031(a)(1) is limited to real property for real property; section 1031(a)(3) sets the 45-day identification and 180-day completion rules. Stocks, bonds and funds are not like-kind real property.

figures.claim: Santa Clara County: over 3,200 tax rate areas; maximum basic ad valorem rate 1% of net taxable value, higher totals from voter-approved general obligation bonds; special assessments are flat direct charges not based on assessed value
figures.note: County Assessor glossary entries 'TRA', 'Tax Rates' and 'Special Assessments' read 15 Nov 2026. The parcels' own TRA numbers and exact rates are on each secured tax bill and are deliberately not published.

figures.claim: For calendar year 2026, the first $19,000 of gifts to any person (other than gifts of future interests in property) are not included in the total amount of taxable gifts under 26 U.S.C. 2503 made during that year
figures.note: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 4.42(1) read directly from the official IRS PDF on 16 Nov 2026. $19,000 is a government-published amount and a multiple of $10, so the site's $10 display rule is not broken.

figures.claim: Annual per-donee gift exclusion for calendar year 2026
figures.note: Corroborates GIFT-ANNUAL-2026 from the other official document: IR-2026-133 (5 Nov 2026) states the 2027 amount and that it is 'up from $19,000 for calendar year 2026', while Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §4.42(1) states the 2026 rule itself. Two sources are kept because the page cites both.

figures.claim: Annual per-donee gift exclusion for calendar year 2027
figures.note: IR-2026-133, 'Estate Tax Exclusion' heading: 'For calendar year 2027, the first $20,000 of gifts to any person are not included in the total amount of taxable gifts made during the year - up from $19,000 for calendar year 2026.' The release cites Rev. Proc. 2026-35 for the 2027 adjustments.

figures.claim: Gift exclusion for a spouse who is not a U.S. citizen, calendar year 2026
figures.note: IR-2026-133 gives $201,000 for 2027, 'up from $194,000' for 2026. The larger figure is the point: an unlimited marital deduction does not apply to a non-citizen spouse.

figures.claim: Gift exclusion for a spouse who is not a U.S. citizen, calendar year 2027
figures.note: IR-2026-133 (Nov. 5, 2026), annual exclusion for gifts to a non-citizen spouse, 2027.

figures.claim: Federal estate tax return and payment are due 9 months after the date of death
figures.note: The 07/2026 Form 706 instructions state the estate and GST taxes are due within 9 months of the date of death. An extension of time to file does not extend the time to pay.

figures.claim: Form 4768 filed by the original due date gives an automatic 6-month extension of time to file the estate tax return
figures.note: The 02/2020 Form 4768 instructions state the extension to file is automatically granted when Part I is properly completed and filed on or before the due date.

figures.claim: Form 4768 Part III extension of time to pay may not exceed 12 months; reasonable-cause extensions are granted 1 year at a time up to a maximum of 10 years (4 years for a deficiency)
figures.official_exact: 12 months at a time; up to 10 years (4 years for a deficiency)
figures.display_rounded: 12 months at a time; up to 10 years
figures.note: The 02/2020 Form 4768 instructions state that an extension to pay does not extend the time to file and that interest runs on unpaid tax regardless of any extension.

figures.claim: Form 8971 and its Schedule A statement are due within 30 days after the Form 706 due date (including extensions), with a copy to the IRS
figures.note: Consistent basis reporting: the beneficiary’s basis must be consistent with the estate tax value reported on Form 706. Read from the 07/2026 instructions on 17 Nov 2026.

figures.claim: San Francisco transfer tax tiers (Article 12-C), applied to the entire consideration
figures.note: Read 17 Nov 2026 from the Assessor-Recorder official fee schedule (schedule dated Jan 1, 2026). A Transfer Tax Affidavit must accompany any document where transfer tax is due or an exemption is claimed.

figures.claim: San Francisco document recording fees: $14.00 first page, $3.00 additional page; SB2 $75 per parcel capped at $225 per transaction and exempt when transfer tax is paid; $20.00 PCOR; $10.00 monument fee on deeds subject to transfer tax
figures.official_exact: $14.00 first page; $3.00 additional page; $75 SB2 per parcel ($225 cap); $20.00 PCOR; $10.00 monument
figures.note: Read 17 Nov 2026 from the Assessor-Recorder official fee schedule.

figures.claim: Santa Clara County recording fees: $102.00 first page of a standard-size document (including $75 SB2, $2 AB1466 restrictive-covenants and a $10 fraud-prevention fee, with the $10 subtracted when the document is subject to documentary transfer tax), $3.00 additional page, $10.00 monument fee, $20.00 PCOR fee
figures.official_exact: $102.00 first page ($92.00 when documentary transfer tax is paid); $3.00 additional page; $10.00 monument; $20.00 PCOR
figures.note: Read 17 Nov 2026 from the county Clerk-Recorder fee schedule and fee pages.

figures.claim: Santa Clara County secured property-tax calendar: bills mailed in October; first installment due November 1 and delinquent after December 10; second due February 1 and delinquent after April 10; June 30 last day to pay without additional penalties; taxes are a lien on January 1
figures.official_exact: Nov 1 / Dec 10; Feb 1 / Apr 10; Jun 30; lien Jan 1
figures.note: Read 17 Nov 2026 from the Department of Tax and Collections published calendar; the delinquency dates match the state code sections used on the timeline.

figures.claim: Rent the living paths are credited at 25 years on the synthetic example inputs, and its share of the live path's total. This is a MODEL OUTPUT, not an official amount: it is recorded here so the published disclosure can be checked against the engine, and it is deliberately not marked verified against a government source.
figures.note: Derived by scripts/test-imputed-rent.py from analysis_model.simulate(..., imputed_rent_mo=0) versus the default. The guide's prose treats it as an assumption, never as a verified figure. Do not add a source_url to this record.

figures.claim: Recovery period for residential rental property under the general depreciation system (alternative system: 30 years)
figures.note: Pub. 527 (2025), Table of recovery periods: 'Residential rental property (buildings or structures) and structural components such as furnaces, waterpipes, venting, etc. | 27.5 years | 30 years'.

figures.claim: Mid-month convention for all residential rental property
figures.note: Pub. 527 (2025): 'A mid-month convention is used for all residential rental property and nonresidential real property. Under this convention, you treat all property placed in service, or disposed of, during any month as placed in service, or disposed of, at the midpoint of that month.'

figures.claim: Required method for residential rental property, and the first-year limit
figures.official_exact: Straight line, mid-month, first year limited to months in use
figures.display_rounded: Straight line, mid-month, first year limited to months in use
figures.note: Pub. 527 (2025): 'You must use the straight line method and a mid-month convention for residential rental property. In the first year that you claim depreciation for residential rental property, you can claim depreciation only for the number of months the property is in use.'

figures.claim: Publication 946 Appendix A carries the 27.5-year mid-month straight-line percentage table
figures.official_exact: Table A-6, 27.5 years, years 1-29 by month placed in service
figures.display_rounded: Table A-6, 27.5 years, years 1-29 by month placed in service
figures.note: Pub. 946 (2025), Appendix A summary: 'Table A-6 is for Residential Rental Property using Mid-Month Convention and Straight Line depreciation--27.5 Years and lists the percentages for years 1 through 29 by month placed in service.'

figures.claim: Land cannot be depreciated
figures.note: Pub. 527 (2025): 'You can’t depreciate the cost of land because land generally doesn’t wear out, become obsolete, or get used up.'

figures.claim: When depreciation begins for rental property
figures.official_exact: Ready and available for its specific use
figures.display_rounded: Ready and available for its specific use
figures.note: Pub. 527 (2025): 'You begin to depreciate your rental property when you place it in service for the production of income.' and 'You place property in service in a rental activity when it is ready and available for a specific use in that activity.'

figures.claim: Basis for depreciation where property changed from personal use to rental use
figures.official_exact: Lesser of adjusted basis or FMV at the change of use
figures.display_rounded: Lesser of adjusted basis or FMV at the change of use
figures.note: Pub. 527 (2025): 'If you used the property for personal purposes before changing it to rental use, its basis for depreciation is the lesser of its adjusted basis or its FMV when you change it to rental use.'

figures.claim: Depreciation reduces basis for gain or loss on a later sale
figures.official_exact: Basis is reduced by depreciation allowed or allowable
figures.display_rounded: Basis is reduced by depreciation allowed or allowable
figures.note: Pub. 527 (2025): 'Depreciation reduces your basis for figuring gain or loss on a later sale or exchange.' Depreciation stops when the yearly deductions, including amounts allowed but not claimed, equal cost or other basis.

figures.claim: Maximum federal rate on unrecaptured section 1250 gain
figures.note: IRS Topic 409 (read 17 Nov 2026): 'The portion of any unrecaptured section 1250 gain from selling section 1250 real property is taxed at a maximum 25% rate.' The same page lists 0%, 15% and 20% for most net capital gain.

figures.claim: Schedule D, line 19, and the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet apply to a disposition of section 1250 property held more than one year
figures.note: Instructions for Schedule D (Form 1040) (2025), line 19: 'You sold or otherwise disposed of section 1250 property (generally, real property that you depreciated) held more than 1 year.'

figures.claim: Form 4797 is where the sale of depreciable business or rental property is reported
figures.note: Instructions for Form 4797 (2025), Purpose of Form: sales, exchanges and involuntary conversions of business property and of property used to produce rent or royalty income.

figures.claim: Maximum gain excluded on the sale of a main home
figures.note: Pub. 523 (2025), Introduction: 'you may exclude the first $250,000 of gain from the sale of your home from your income and avoid paying taxes on it. The exclusion is increased to $500,000 for a married couple filing jointly.'

figures.claim: Ownership requirement for the maximum exclusion
figures.official_exact: 24 months out of the last 5 years
figures.display_rounded: 24 months out of the last 5 years
figures.note: Pub. 523 (2025), Eligibility Step 2: 'If you owned the home for at least 24 months (2 years) out of the last 5 years leading up to the date of sale (date of the closing), you meet the ownership requirement.'

figures.claim: Residence requirement for the maximum exclusion
figures.official_exact: 24 months of the previous 5 years, each spouse individually
figures.display_rounded: 24 months of the previous 5 years, each spouse individually
figures.note: Pub. 523 (2025), Eligibility Step 3: 'If you owned the home and used it as your residence for at least 24 months of the previous 5 years, you meet the residence requirement.' The page adds that each spouse must meet this test individually for the full joint exclusion.

figures.claim: How often the exclusion can be used
figures.note: Pub. 523 (2025), Eligibility Step 4: 'You may take the exclusion only once during a 2-year period.'

figures.claim: The exclusion applies only to a main home, and a person has only one at a time
figures.official_exact: One main home at a time
figures.display_rounded: One main home at a time
figures.note: Pub. 523 (2025): 'An individual has only one main home at a time.' Where more than one home is owned or lived in, a facts-and-circumstances test decides which is the main home.

figures.claim: Gain equal to depreciation after 6 May 1997 cannot be excluded
figures.official_exact: Depreciation after 6 May 1997 is never excluded
figures.display_rounded: Depreciation after 6 May 1997 is never excluded
figures.note: Pub. 523 (2025), Recapturing Depreciation: 'you cannot exclude the part of your gain equal to any depreciation allowed or allowable as a deduction for periods after May 6, 1997.'

figures.claim: Gain allocated to nonqualified use after 2008 is not excludable
figures.official_exact: Periods after 2008 when the property was not a main home
figures.display_rounded: Periods after 2008 when the property was not a main home
figures.note: Pub. 523 (2025), Business or Rental Use of Home: 'Nonqualified use means any period after 2008 when neither you nor your spouse (or former spouse) used the property as your main home, with certain exceptions.' Worksheet 3 Section B allocates by nonuse days divided by days owned.

figures.claim: The part of the 5-year window after the last qualified use is not nonqualified use
figures.official_exact: Post-residence rental inside the window is not nonqualified use
figures.display_rounded: Post-residence rental inside the window is not nonqualified use
figures.note: Pub. 523 (2025) lists the exception and illustrates it with the Taylor example, citing section 121(b)(5)(C)(ii): renting the home after moving out produces no nonqualified use, though the depreciation is still recaptured.

figures.claim: The IRS worked example: rented first, then lived there, then sold
figures.note: Pub. 523 (2025) prints the Finley example with these figures. This site's worksheet code reproduces every one of them; see scripts/test-tax-realism.py.

figures.claim: The IRS worked example: lived there first, then rented, then sold
figures.note: Pub. 523 (2025) prints the Taylor example with these figures. This site's worksheet code reproduces every one of them; see scripts/test-tax-realism.py.
